notes: A chart of accounts built for a Ghanaian business. Until now there was one chart to start from: the University of Cape Coast's IPSAS chart — 840 accounts, 92 of them naming UCC, alongside union deductions, halls of residence and a superannuation account. For a university that is exactly right; for a trading company, a restaurant, a clinic or an NGO it is somebody else's chart, and it is the first thing you meet when you open an account picker. There is now a general Ghanaian chart of 186 accounts, and the setup wizard asks which one you want. Short is the point — a chart too long to post to is the commonest way one fails. Ghana's statutory deductions each have their own account: PAYE, SSNIT tiers 1, 2 and 3, output and input VAT, withholding tax, withholding VAT, the tourism levy and a community fund levy you can rename — so the returns this app already produces have somewhere obvious to post to, and the schedule and the ledger agree without anyone reconciling them by hand. Mobile money sits beside the bank accounts, because for a Ghanaian business it is one. Every depreciable class carries all three accounts the fixed-asset register needs — cost, accumulated depreciation and the charge — so nothing depreciates into nowhere; land does not depreciate and software amortises. Hospitality, school fees and donor grants with restricted and unrestricted funds are all in it, so one chart serves a business, a school and an NGO. NOTHING CHANGES FOR EXISTING BOOKS: this is the chart you are OFFERED when setting up a new set of books, charts already loaded are untouched, and the university chart is still on the list.
